provenance: Four condition contrasts approved by the student on 2026-10-18. Exact fixture text and expectations are AI-authored under that scope, not scanner-derived or independently adjudicated.
condition: A directly decorated tool passes its caller-supplied string URL directly as the initial requests.get destination without a fixed destination restriction.
limitations: Source-condition comparison only; not proof of attacker access, SSRF exploitability, redirect safety or effective network permissions.
No target code imports, installations or execution; example.com destinations are inert fixture text.
The three absent-condition cases do not establish general safety. Fixed URL selection can still have other risks.
One deliberately related development contrast family, not four independent real-world samples. Never held-out evaluation data.

cases.content:
import requests
from langchain_core.tools import tool


@tool
def fetch_resource(url: str) -> str:
    """Fetch the resource selected by the caller."""
    response = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
    return response.text
cases.rationale: The decorated function's URL parameter is passed directly to the request destination. This is the finite source condition, not a demonstrated exploit.

cases.content:
import requests


def fetch_resource() -> str:
    """Fetch one fixed resource."""
    url = "https://example.com/data.txt"
    response = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
    return response.text
cases.rationale: There is no tool decorator or function parameter. The local URL variable is assigned a fixed string. This reduces the public-pilot mismatch to a minimal development contrast.

cases.content:
import requests
from langchain_core.tools import tool


@tool
def fetch_resource() -> str:
    """Fetch one fixed resource."""
    url = "https://example.com/data.txt"
    response = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
    return response.text
cases.rationale: Adding a tool decorator does not introduce a caller-supplied destination. The parameterless function still uses a fixed local URL string.
The caller selects a key in a local fixed URL mapping, not an arbitrary initial destination. Redirects, destination integrity and deployment controls are outside this condition.
